sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the simple act of dwelling in the sukkah affects even the distant encompassing light, raising the question of how change can apply to a level beyond the category of "man" where change is not applicable.

translations.translation: And behold, the explanation of "all the native-born in Israel shall dwell in sukkot"
(simply)
is,
that Israel below
(souls in bodies)
need to dwell in a sukkah
(literally).
And according to the known principle
that all the explanations of that same verse are connected to each other,
it is understood,
that also the matter of dwelling in sukkot in the distant encompassing light is through the literal dwelling in the sukkah.
And based on this,
through Israel dwelling in the sukkah,
a change is also made in the distant encompassing light.
And it needs to be understood,
for it is explained in many places
on the verse,
"For He is not a man, to be consoled,"
that the matter of consolation and regret
(change)
applies only to the aspect of "man,"
but in the aspect of "not man,"
consolation does not apply,
change.
And the reason for this is,
that the matter of change is
(primarily)
in intellect,
for in intellect there is reasoning for this and reasoning for that,
and since "man" is intellect and emotions,
meaning that even the emotions in man are based on intellect,
therefore,
when a change occurs in the intellect, the emotions also change.
But not so a will that is above intellect,
that is, an essential will that has no reason,
not even a hidden reason,
does not change.
And similarly above,
that in the Sefiros of Atzilus and also in the externality of Kesser
(for even the externality of Kesser is included in the aspect of "man"),
change applies,
but in the innerness of Kesser
("not man")
change does not apply.

And based on this, it needs to be understood in this matter, that it is implied from the maamar that through Israel dwelling in the sukkah, even the distant encompassing light is drawn into innerness,
for seemingly,
how can change apply to the distant encompassing light?

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that from the perspective of the Essence of Ein Sof, which transcends the distinction between encompassing and inner light, the encompassing light can become a settled light through Israel's dwelling in the sukkah, revealing the teshuvah of Yom Kippur.

translations.translation: D)
And one can say the explanation of this,
that this that an encompassing light is defined as that which does not come into settlement is as it is from its own side,
but from the side of the Essence of Ein Sof,
regarding which there is no distinction between encompassing and inner,
even the encompassing light can come into settlement.
And through Israel dwelling in the sukkah, they draw from the Essence of Ein Sof,
and through this, even the encompassing lights become settled lights.
And this will be understood according to the known explanation
of the verse,
"At the concealed time of our festival,"
that the matters which
(on Rosh Hashanah and)
on Yom Kippur are in concealment
(covering and concealment),
are revealed on Sukkot.
For from this it is understood,
that the service of "in sukkot you shall dwell" is the revelation of the teshuvah of Yom Kippur,
through which is the drawing from the Essence of Ein Sof
(as will be explained below).
And through the service of "in sukkot you shall dwell,"
the drawing from the Essence of Ein Sof that comes through the teshuvah of Yom Kippur is revealed.
And through this,
even the encompassing lights become settled lights.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the service of dwelling in the sukkah itself involves change, analogous to teshuvah where a person becomes a new reality, and even for tzaddikim this change is included in their will to fulfill the divine purpose.

translations.translation: And according to the known principle
that the service of man
(arousal from below)
through which the drawing is made
(arousal from above)
must be similar to the drawing,
one must add,
that this that through the service of "in sukkot you shall dwell" a change is made above
(that the encompassing lights become settled lights)
is because the service of "in sukkot you shall dwell" pertains
(also)
to the matter of change.
And this will be understood by prefacing,
that the reason
(simply)
for this that through teshuvah all blemishes are rectified is because through teshuvah a person changes and becomes a new reality.
And in the language of the Rambam,
"I am another, and I am not that same person who performed those deeds."
Now, this matter is primarily in simple teshuvah.
But regarding tzaddikim,
even their service of teshuvah, whose matter is that they go out from their previous state and reality,
is forbidden from here,
nevertheless, since tzaddikim desire to do the will of their Master,
and the supernal intention
(the will of their Master)
in the descent of the soul into the body is to come to teshuvah,
behold, in the will of the tzaddikim
(even before their teshuvah)
is included
(in concealment)
also the going out from their reality that comes through teshuvah.
But not so regarding a simple baal teshuvah,
since before
(before the teshuvah)
he was in a state where he did not do the will of the Holy One, blessed be He,
for he committed sins intentionally,
behold, this that he later does teshuvah,
is not a continuation from his previous state,
and through teshuvah he becomes an entirely new reality.
